items.name: Kujur
items.desc: Among the Nuba of the Nuba Mountains, a kujur is a man or woman whose power is granted by God and through whom the Nuba know God. The kujur is the most sacred person, able to bring prosperity and lift suffering after natural crisis; each Nuba tribe has one, and ritual performance differs from tribe to tribe. A council of kujurs appoints the supreme Kujur, the Tabowake, who calls the community to prepare for rain and directs agricultural work.

items.name: The Universal Basilisk
items.desc: A legendary serpent or dragon, the Basilisk is known as the king of serpents, with a gaze and breath so venomous it can kill anything it encounters.

items.name: Bouchkara
items.desc: Bouchkara is a Tunisian bogey figure invoked to frighten disobedient children. The familiar threat is that Bouchkara will put you in her sack if you do not behave; she belongs to the same nursery-terror repertoire as the Ghoula. Tunisian popular articles and Yassine Ellil bilingual Monstres fantastiques tunisiens (2012) list her among the recurring figures of Tunisian oral and written tales.
